title: Runtime surfaces left outside the phase-1/phase-3 rule sets

rules.why: Localized InfoPlist.strings only cover six languages; every other system language falls back to the base Info.plist. Keep the fallback on-brand.
This string is the entry shown in WhatsApp's Linked Devices list.
Template agent names are user-visible when a user creates an agent from a template.
Issue-form labels and descriptions are shown to users filing bugs on GitHub.
The release publishes Nuo-<version>.dmg; the appcast script still downloaded the old name and failed with 404.
The full DMG is built as Nuo-<version>-full.dmg; the upload script looked for the old name.

rules.replace:
import AppKit
import OsaurusRepository
import SwiftUI

rules.why: The in-app installer looked only for the pre-rename helper and installed an `osaurus` symlink. Prefer `nuo`, keep the legacy lookup for one release.

rules.replace:
import Foundation
import OsaurusRepository
import SwiftUI

rules.why: Claude Code's MCP bridge resolved only `Contents/Helpers/osaurus`; prefer `nuo` and keep the legacy fallback.
HTTP error copy still told users to run the pre-rename command.
New theme links are minted as nuo://; the import copy must not show the retired scheme.
The rename turned `an Osaurus ...` into `an Nuo ...`; the article has to follow the new pronunciation.
Tool-call cards emitted a Markdown link on the retired scheme; new links must use nuo://.

Failed/uncatalogued calls humanise the frozen tool id, so `osaurus_config` rendered as `Osaurus config` in the chip. Block form because the replacement needs its own lines to stay under the 120-column limit.

X-OpenRouter-Title carries the app title to the provider, so it is an A-class product self-reference. The file sits in the swift-literals files_exclude because its B-class Osaurus Router/ID copy must stay frozen; this targeted block fixes the one A-class constant that miss left behind (tests already expect Nuo).
